title: Protocol for isolation of adult mouse ear pinnae-derived primary fibroblasts
protocol: Aliquot 5–10 mL of tissue wash buffer into one sterile 15 mL centrifuge tube for each sample.
Maintain centrifuge tubes on ice.
Euthanize each C57BL/6Nia mouse according to the procedures approved by your Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
Spray the mouse with 70% ethanol, ensuring fur on and around the ear pinnae is wet.
Shave as much of the fur on and around each ear pinna as possible using a razor blade.
Cut off each ear pinna with sterilized scissors and transfer tissues to the corresponding centrifuge tube on ice.
Clean tweezers and scissors with ethanol between each animal.
Collect ear pinnae tissue from the remaining mice.
Submerge collected tissue in tissue wash buffer.
Keep centrifuge tubes on ice during collection.
Cut each ear pinna as needed without altering extraction efficiency.
Place both ear pinnae of each animal into a single tube.
Seal 15 mL centrifuge tubes with parafilm if tissues will be shipped.
Maintain sealed tubes at 4°C for up to three days before the next step.
Prepare 6-well suspension plates.
Fill two wells each with 5 mL of 70% ethanol for each independent animal.
Fill one well with 5 mL of tissue wash buffer for each independent animal.
Transfer tissues and some buffer to a separate set of empty 6-well suspension plates.
Clean tweezers with 70% ethanol prior to transferring each independent sample.
Sequentially wash ear pinnae twice in 70% ethanol.
Wash ear pinnae for 5 minutes at 18°C–25°C using a rocker in the first ethanol-filled well.
Transfer ear pinnae to the second ethanol-filled well and wash again for 5 minutes at 18°C–25°C using a rocker.
Remove excess ethanol from ear pinnae using tweezers and press against a clean paper towel.
Immerse ear pinnae in tissue wash buffer immediately after removing excess ethanol.
Store plates temporarily at 4°C until ear pinnae are ready to be diced into finer pieces.
Dice the washed ear pinnae into smaller pieces.
Culture diced ear pinnae with 3 mL of initial growth media to promote fibroblast adherence.
Transfer only the tissue from both ear pinnae to a sterile 10 cm petri dish.
Add a few drops of tissue wash buffer to keep the tissue moist.
Trim any remaining fur with an autoclaved razor blade if needed.
Dice the tissue into fragments using a second pair of autoclaved razor blades, aiming for sizes of 1–3 mm x 1–3 mm.
Resuspend the diced tissue with 3 mL of initial growth media.
Transfer the resuspended tissue to a 10 cm tissue culture dish.
Gently agitate the plate to distribute tissue fragments.
Incubate the plate in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Continue trimming, dicing, transferring, and incubating the remaining samples.
Incubate the plates without disturbance for three days.
Check plates after three days for primary fibroblasts under the microscope.
Discard immediately if signs of microbial contamination are observed, such as media turning yellow or opaque or visible fungal outgrowths.
Remove the remaining media.
Gently add 10 mL of fresh initial growth media.
Minimize agitation of tissue fragments attached to the plate.
Continue incubating the plates in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Remove old media after seven days.
Add fresh initial growth media again.
Replace initial growth media every 2–3 days for up to another week.
Passage cultures several times before storage or usage if "myocyte-like" cells are present.
Discard samples with no or few dense clusters after two weeks.
Aspirate the culture media during Passage 0.
Wash cells twice with 2.5 mL of HBSS.
Add 3 mL of 0.25% trypsin to each plate and incubate for ~6 min at 37°C.
Gently tap plates if a few clusters of cells remain attached after trypsinization.
Neutralize the trypsin with 6 mL of 10% FBS-containing media.
Transfer solutions to sterile 15 mL centrifuge tubes.
Spin down the solutions at 500 × g and at 18°C–25°C for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 9 mL of expansion growth media.
Attach 70 μm MACS SmartStrainers to sterile 15 mL centrifuge tubes.
Pre-wet the strainers with 1 mL of expansion growth media.
Pass the 9 mL of cell-tissue suspensions through the strainers.
Allow tissues and cells to separate by gravity filtration for a few seconds.
Transfer the filtered cell suspensions to 10 cm tissue culture dishes.
Designate these cells as Passage 1.
Incubate the plates in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Replace the media every 2–3 days until cells reach confluency.
Carry out the second passage at ~17 days.
Passage the cells 1:4 without using a strainer.
Split confluent cells from Passage 2 among four plates for Passage 3.
Freeze and store the cells long-term once they reach approximately 90% confluency.
Fill Mr. Frosty Boxes with 2-Propanol if not already filled, replacing alcohol after fifth use.
Dissociate cells by trypsinization, neutralize trypsin, combine cell suspensions in a 50 mL centrifuge tube corresponding to the same sample.
Spin down cells and aspirate supernatants.
Resuspend cells in freshly prepared freezing media at 1 mL per plate.
Aliquot cell suspensions into cryovials at 1 mL per vial.
Place vials in Mr. Frosty Boxes and store at -80°C.
Transfer vials from the -80°C freezer to a liquid nitrogen tank after chilling for 12-16 hours for long-term storage.
Pre-warm a bottle of long-term culture media in a water or bead bath at 37°C.
Rapidly thaw the contents of frozen vials of fibroblasts in a 37°C water bath.
Spray the vials liberally with 70% ethanol before transferring to the biological hood.
Combine 1 mL of each cell suspension with 10 mL of pre-warmed long-term culture media in a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Pellet cells at 500 × g in a centrifuge at 18°C–25°C for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 10 mL of pre-warmed long-term culture media.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a 10 cm tissue culture dish.
After 24 h, passage and use the cells for experiments.
Use 0.05% trypsin to minimize cell stress (optional).
Confirm purity of the obtained cell culture using flow cytometry (optional).
Wash the fibroblast layer twice using 10 mL DPBS.
Apply 2 mL of 0.05% trypsin to detach cells.
Incubate for 7 min in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Neutralize the trypsin with 8 mL of long-term culture media (10% FBS-containing media).
Collect detached cells in a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Pellet cells at 500 × g and at 18°C–25°C for 10 min in a centrifuge.
Wash cells with 10 mL of resuspension buffer.
Pellet cells at 500 × g and at 18°C–25°C for 10 min in a centrifuge.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of resuspension buffer.
Count cells and determine cell viability using Trypan Blue exclusion and a Countess cell counting apparatus.
Aliquot 300,000 cells per culture into 5 mL polystyrene round-bottom tubes for staining.
Pellet cells at 500 × g and at 18°C–25°C for 10 min in a centrifuge.
Resuspend cells in 50 μL of flow cytometry staining buffer.
Block cells by incubating at 4°C for 10 min.
Prepare 50 μL of a 2× antibody solution in flow cytometry staining buffer for each sample to be stained.
Add 50 μL of 2× antibody solution to the 50 μL of blocked cells.
Stain cells by incubating at 4°C for 20 min in the dark.
Wash away excess antibody by adding 2 mL of resuspension buffer and then pellet cells by centrifuging at 500 × g and at 18°C–25°C for 10 min.
Resuspend the pellet in 2 mL of resuspension buffer for a second wash, and again pellet cells by centrifuging at 500 × g and at 18°C–25°C for 10 min.
Resuspend cells in 100 μL of resuspension buffer per 100,000 cells.
Optional: Add 1 μL of propidium iodide (PI) per 100 μL of sample to quantify and exclude dead cells.
Run samples through a MACSQuant 10 flow cytometer.
Unstained samples and single-stained samples are used to set appropriate gates that have clear positive and negative populations.
